messages:
alex_g: FYI customer reported that after their Okta rule changes some users are getting a 403 when opening Project > Settings in the console. They can see org list but clicking into the project yields permission denied. I have their repro steps and token snippets.
sanjay: thanks. do we know whether they’re using SAML or OIDC? any recent claim/transformation? :thinking:
alex_g: OIDC. They said Admin renamed a claim mapping two days ago to standardize names. i asked them for the id_token and here’s the decoded payload they pasted (sanitized):
```
{
  "sub": "00u1abcd2EFGH3ij4kl5",
  "email": "dev@acme.example",
  "email_verified": true,
  "iss": "https://acme.okta.com/oauth2/default",
  "aud": "0oa1exampleclientid",
  "iat": 1670000000,
  "exp": 1670003600,
  "groups": null
}
```
They previously had a custom claim `roles` with org/project roles but the transform was removed. now the console doesn’t see any role claim and denies access.
maria: that aligns w/ our auth flow — console checks for either `roles` claim or mapped `groups` claim (configured at org level). if neither present we map to no access. did they use Okta Attribute Statements -> Transform or a claims rule? emily: i can confirm our code paths: for OIDC we accept `roles`, `x-roles`, or `groups` (case-insensitive). if none present, we return 403 when hitting project-level endpoints.
alex_g: customer tried re-adding the claim but says Okta transformation returns empty array. they ran a test user and got groups: [] in the token.
idp-bot: automated-note: recent known issue: okta transform removal may produce empty/null claims when mapping to JWT. See internal KB #IDP-92.
sanjay: recommended next steps to the customer: 1) check Okta app mapping to ensure attribute is a list and not a string; 2) temporarily add a custom claim `roles` with a static value for one test user to confirm console accepts it; 3) if using group filter, ensure user is assigned to the group and the filter matches exact group name. asked them to paste the app config screenshot.
emily: quick workaround: support can invite the specific user as a project member via the org-admin route (we can create a one-time invite link), but warn that this bypasses SSO claim mapping and is not ideal long-term. also logging added to auth-service to surface missing claim names in /debug for support.
maria: if customer confirms app config is correct but token still lacks claim, escalate to idp-infra to check transform execution in Okta. marking this thread for eng-security FYI. @eng-security please advise if we should accept alternate claim names for a short period. :eyes:
alex_g: customer will try the static `roles` claim test and post results. I’ll update when they respond. thanks all.
